enroll.privacySummary: How is my data handled? (privacy notice)
enroll.privacyNotice:
Providing your details is not required by law and is entirely voluntary; without them we cannot enroll you in the club and issue your loyalty card. The details you provide (name, mobile number, and birthday — if you chose to share it) are stored in this business's customer database (the data controller) and processed on its behalf by PunchMe, the digital loyalty-card service, for managing the club, awarding stamps and rewards, and issuing a card to your digital wallet (Apple Wallet / Google Wallet) via wallet infrastructure providers. Your data is not shared with other third parties except as required by law.

You have the right to access data about you, to request correction or deletion of data that is inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated (sections 13–14 of the Israeli Privacy Protection Law, 1981), and to demand in writing deletion from the direct-mailing database (section 17F).

proof.title: Your regulars are worth more than you think
proof.lead: Three numbers worth knowing before you decide anything. Each one links to where it came from.

stats.claim: Regulars generate about six times more annual revenue than one-time customers.
stats.context: Square counted a regular as someone who visits at least four times a year, across seven years of US small-business transactions.
stats.source: Square Local Economy Report, March 2026 (US data)

stats.claim: Winning a new customer costs five to twenty-five times more than keeping one you already have.
stats.context: A broad estimate, not a controlled study, which is why it's a range.

stats.claim: are less likely to join a loyalty program that makes them download an app.
stats.context: 79% said they'd sooner join one with no physical card to carry, and a wallet pass is neither. The same survey found people wary of programs that collect personal data. Here, only the mobile number is required.

calculator.title: How many regulars does PunchMe need to pay for itself?
calculator.lead: Fewer than you would think. Move the sliders to match your shop — nothing you type here leaves your browser.

items.q: Does my customer need to download an app?
items.a: No. The card is a wallet pass, so it opens straight into the Apple Wallet or Google Wallet already on their phone. They scan your QR code once and it's saved — nothing to install, no account to create, no password to forget.

items.q: How do I add a stamp?
items.a: You scan the QR code on the customer's pass. It takes about as long as handing back a receipt, and the stamp appears on their card straight away.

items.q: What happens if they change phones?
items.a: Their stamps are stored against their card on our side, not on the phone itself, so the count is never lost. Moving the pass onto a new handset isn't automatic yet — message us and we'll sort it out.

items.q: What does it cost, and when am I charged?
items.a: Designing your card, previewing it on your own phone and using the dashboard are free for as long as you like. You're charged ₪99 a month only when you activate the card for real customers.

items.q: Can I change the design after I launch?
items.a: Yes, and you do it yourself, whenever you like. Open Card Studio in your dashboard and change the colors, the stamp count or the reward. When you save, the new design goes out to every card already in your customers' wallets.

items.q: Does it work on both iPhone and Android?
items.a: Yes. iPhone customers get an Apple Wallet pass and Android customers get a Google Wallet pass. Both update the same way, and you scan them the same way.

styleGuide.title: Lightbox
styleGuide.lead: The page is a lit sign: warm panels with light behind them, soft dark letters, and one coral thing to press. Every page the redesign moves over is built from what is on this one.

toolbar.label: How the guide is shown
toolbar.reducedMotionHint: The gentler motion a device set to reduce motion gets.

measure.fillOnly: A fill only, so it always carries an ink label

colour.title: Colour
colour.lead: Every text colour on every ground it can sit on, measured here in the browser rather than copied from a comment. Text needs 4.5:1; a field's edge, a focus ring or a state needs 3:1.
colour.rule: Coral is a fill and never text, and nothing else on a screen is a warm fill: a warning or an error is its words and its icon.
colour.dayLead: A warm wall with lit panels on it.
colour.nightLead: The street after closing. The panels go dark.
colour.litLead: What keeps its light after dark: the pass, the QR code, the brief and the scan's answer.
colour.lightLead: The same by day and at night, and always under ink.

type.title: Type
type.lead: Rubik 500 for display and the interface, Assistant for running text, and Rubik's tabular figures for numbers. Each line is measured as it renders, so Hebrew shows its own leading.

shape.title: Shape, depth and light
shape.lead: Generous and soft. Depth comes from light rather than from shadow.
shape.depthLead: By day a lit panel carries a highlight inside its top edge and a soft warm drop. At night it loses both, and its own edge is enough.
shape.lift: Lifted: a dialog, a sheet, a toast
shape.band: The band today's violet brief becomes
shape.field: The field the landing page stages things in

controls.title: Controls
controls.lead: Every control is 44px wherever a thumb goes, shows a ring on the keyboard, and keeps coral for the one thing to press.
controls.linkButton: A link that looks like a button
controls.fieldsLead: A label always, a hint when it helps, and an error that says what is wrong and how to put it right. Phone numbers read left to right in either language.
controls.filterChipsLead: One of several ways to narrow a list, each with its count. They wrap onto a second line rather than scroll sideways, the chosen one is filled, and one with nothing in it can't be picked.

panels.title: Panels
panels.lead: Lightboxes on a wall. Each one is lit, or keeps its light at night, according to what it holds.
panels.panel: Lit by day and unlit at night. Most of the dashboard is this.
panels.lit: Keeps its light at night: the QR code, a message preview.
panels.band: The dashboard's one loud surface, lit in both themes.
panels.field: The landing page's light, brightest at the centre.

content.title: Content
content.lead: The pieces pages are made of. Every number is real and every word is the product's own.
content.figuresLead: Printed, never counted up, and a figure that makes a claim carries its source.
content.noticeLead: What a page has to say in place: done, worth knowing, or wrong. An icon and words on a plain panel, never a warm fill. A lit one keeps its light at night.

motion.title: Motion
motion.lead: Things arrive by light, not by travel. Interface motion stays under 300ms, and with reduced motion it is gentler, not gone.
motion.lightsOnLead: A panel's light fades up over 240ms while it rises 8px at most. Reduced: full strength in 150ms, no travel.
motion.stampLead: The product's one gesture: 340ms on the overshoot, pressed down and lifted. Reduced: it appears at its final size.

overlays.title: Dialogs, sheets and toasts
overlays.lead: A dialog asks a question that has to be answered first. A sheet holds work beside the page. A toast confirms what was just done, and is never how a result, a refusal or a loss is said.
overlays.toastLead: A confirmation goes after 4 seconds, counted only while it can be read. An error stays until it is dismissed.

stage.title: The card on its own wallpaper
stage.lead: How the owner's card is staged in the dashboard: on a wallpaper made from its own colours, under the message it brings. It is the customer's phone, so it looks the same at night.
stage.example: An example: a sample card, named for its trade.
stage.summary: The {{trade}} card on a lock screen, with {{filled}} of {{total}} stamps.

snap.title: The scan's answer
snap.lead: At the counter, Scan answers like a photo snap: a flash of the panels' own light, the answer settling under it, the newest stamp landing, all over in 300ms. With reduced motion, a 150ms fade and a soft glow.
